name: simple-workflow
title: Simple Workflow
description: Pick one ClinicalTrials.gov NCT id from a fixed list of five studies, download every document the study has posted (protocol, SAP, ICF), then have an agent extract CDISC USDM study-definition metadata from those documents for human review.

steps.name: Select Study
steps.description: Choose the NCT id of the study this run works on.

params.name: nctId
params.description: ClinicalTrials.gov registry identifier of the selected study

steps.name: Fetch Study Documents
steps.description: Ask the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API which documents the selected study has posted and download each one into the step output.

steps.name: Generate USDM Metadata
steps.description: AI. Reads the protocol (and SAP / ICF when present) downloaded by Fetch Study Documents out of the run workspace, extracts the study definition, and writes CDISC USDM v3.0.0 metadata as usdm.json, with usdm-provenance.json for page-level traceability and usdm-summary.md for the reviewer. All three land in /output as step Output Files and in /workspace/usdm/ on the run branch. On a revise re-entry, reads the reviewer's comment from the review-usdm step and corrects only the flagged items.

agent.prompt:
You are a CDISC USDM data engineer. Extract the study definition from the study documents downloaded by the previous step and emit it as USDM v3.0.0 metadata.

# 1. Find the source documents

The `fetch-documents` step downloaded every document ClinicalTrials.gov posted for this study and committed them into the run workspace. Their metadata is in your Input Data under `steps['fetch-documents'].documents[]` — each entry has `filename`, `typeAbbrev`, `label`, `date`, `sizeBytes`.

Locate the actual PDF bytes FIRST, before any other work:

```
find /workspace /data -name '*.pdf' 2>/dev/null
```

They are expected under `/workspace/.mediforce/output/fetch-documents/`.

If that finds no PDF, STOP. Write to /output/result.json:
`{"error": "no source PDFs found", "searched": ["/workspace", "/data"], "workspaceListing": "<output of: ls -R /workspace | head -200>"}`
and make that file your result. Do NOT fabricate USDM content from the ClinicalTrials.gov metadata in your Input Data — an empty-handed failure with a directory listing is far more useful than invented study data.

Classify the documents by `typeAbbrev`:
- `Prot` — study protocol. PRIMARY source.
- `Prot_SAP` — combined protocol + SAP. PRIMARY source.
- `SAP` — statistical analysis plan. Secondary: objectives, endpoints, estimands, analysis populations.
- `ICF` — informed consent form. Lowest priority; eligibility wording only, and only if the protocol is unusable.

# 2. Extract text

```
pdftotext -layout <pdf> /output/<basename>.txt
```

`-layout` preserves table structure, which the arms / epochs / schedule-of-activities tables depend on. Protocols run 100–300 pages: do NOT read a whole file linearly. Grep for section headings and read the sections you need — title page, synopsis or protocol summary, objectives and endpoints, study design and schema, eligibility criteria, study treatments / interventions, schedule of activities.

Record the 1-based PDF page number for everything you extract. `pdftotext` emits form feeds (\f) between pages, so page N is the Nth form-feed-delimited block.

# 3. Build the USDM JSON

Target **USDM v3.0.0**. Keep real USDM class and attribute names. Write this envelope to `usdm.json`:

```json
{
  "usdmVersion": "3.0.0",
  "systemName": "mediforce simple-workflow generate-usdm",
  "study": {
    "id": "Study_1",
    "name": "<sponsor protocol number, or the NCT id if none>",
    "label": "<brief title>",
    "description": "<1-3 sentence description>",
    "versions": [
      {
        "id": "StudyVersion_1",
        "versionIdentifier": "<protocol version / amendment number from the title page>",
        "rationale": "<why this version exists, if the document states it; else null>",
        "titles": [
          { "id": "StudyTitle_1", "text": "<verbatim official title>", "type": { "id": "Code_1", "code": "C207616", "codeSystem": "http://www.cdisc.org", "codeSystemVersion": null, "decode": "Official Study Title" } }
        ],
        "studyIdentifiers": [
          { "id": "StudyIdentifier_1", "studyIdentifier": "<NCT id>", "studyIdentifierScope": { "id": "Organization_1", "name": "ClinicalTrials.gov", "type": { "id": "Code_2", "code": "C93453", "codeSystem": "http://www.cdisc.org", "codeSystemVersion": null, "decode": "Study Registry" } } }
        ],
        "studyType": { "...Code...": "Interventional or Observational" },
        "studyPhase": { "...AliasCode wrapping a Code...": "e.g. C15602 / Phase III Trial" },
        "businessTherapeuticAreas": [],
        "studyDesigns": [
          {
            "id": "StudyDesign_1",
            "name": "<short design name>",
            "label": "<design label>",
            "description": "<the design sentence from the synopsis>",
            "studyType": "<Code>",
            "therapeuticAreas": [],
            "interventionModel": "<Code: Parallel / Crossover / Single Group / Factorial>",
            "blindingSchema": "<AliasCode: Open Label / Double Blind / ...>",
            "trialIntentTypes": [],
            "trialTypes": [],
            "arms": [ { "id": "Arm_1", "name": "...", "label": "...", "description": "...", "type": "<Code: Experimental / Placebo Comparator / ...>", "dataOriginDescription": null, "dataOriginType": null } ],
            "epochs": [ { "id": "Epoch_1", "name": "Screening", "label": "...", "description": "...", "type": "<Code>", "previousId": null, "nextId": "Epoch_2" } ],
            "elements": [ { "id": "StudyElement_1", "name": "...", "label": "...", "description": "..." } ],
            "studyCells": [ { "id": "StudyCell_1", "armId": "Arm_1", "epochId": "Epoch_1", "elementIds": ["StudyElement_1"] } ],
            "objectives": [
              { "id": "Objective_1", "name": "Primary Objective 1", "description": "...", "text": "<verbatim>", "level": "<Code: Primary / Secondary / Exploratory>",
                "endpoints": [ { "id": "Endpoint_1_1", "name": "...", "text": "<verbatim>", "purpose": "...", "level": "<Code>" } ] }
            ],
            "population": { "id": "StudyDesignPopulation_1", "name": "...", "description": "...", "plannedEnrollmentNumber": { "minValue": null, "maxValue": null }, "plannedSex": [], "plannedAge": null, "criterionIds": ["EligibilityCriterion_1"] },
            "eligibilityCriteria": [ { "id": "EligibilityCriterion_1", "name": "INCL 1", "label": "...", "identifier": "1", "category": "<Code: Inclusion / Exclusion>", "text": "<verbatim criterion text>" } ],
            "studyInterventions": [ { "id": "StudyIntervention_1", "name": "...", "label": "...", "description": "...", "role": "<Code>", "type": "<Code: Drug / Device / Procedure / ...>", "minimumResponseDuration": null, "codes": [] } ],
            "encounters": [],
            "activities": []
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "documentedBy": [ { "id": "StudyDefinitionDocument_1", "name": "...", "label": "<source PDF filename>", "type": "<Code: Protocol / Statistical Analysis Plan / Informed Consent>", "language": "en" } ]
  }
}
```

Every `Code` is `{ "id", "code", "codeSystem", "codeSystemVersion", "decode" }`. An `AliasCode` is `{ "id", "standardCode": <Code> }`.

Rules that are not negotiable:

1. **Never invent content.** Every `text`, `description`, and `name` must come from the source documents. If the protocol does not state something, set it to `null` and add an entry to `unresolved` in result.json. A sparse-but-true USDM beats a full-but-fabricated one, and the reviewer's job is to catch exactly this.
2. **Codes:** use the real CDISC CT code when you are confident of it (e.g. `C15602` = Phase III Trial, `C98388` = Interventional Study). When you are not confident, set `"code": null` and keep `"decode"` as the verbatim source wording, then add an `unresolved` entry. Do not guess code values.
3. **Referential integrity:** every `armId`, `epochId`, `elementIds[]`, and `criterionIds[]` must resolve to an `id` you actually declared. Before writing the file, verify this — walk the reference fields and check each target exists. State the result in result.json's `integrityCheck`.
4. **Epoch chaining:** `previousId` / `nextId` must form one consistent chain across `epochs` in study order.
5. **studyCells** is the arm × epoch matrix. Emit one cell per (arm, epoch) pair the design actually uses, not the full cross product if the design does not use it.
6. `activities` and `encounters` (the schedule of activities) are BEST EFFORT. Populate them only if the SoA table extracted legibly. If it did not, leave both as `[]` and add an `unresolved` entry saying so — do not reconstruct a schedule from prose.

# 4. Traceability

Write `usdm-provenance.json`:

```json
{ "nctId": "...",
  "entries": [ { "path": "study.versions[0].titles[0].text", "sourceFile": "NCT..._Prot_000.pdf", "page": 1, "quote": "<short verbatim quote, <= 200 chars>" } ] }
```

Provenance is REQUIRED for: every title, every studyIdentifier, studyType, studyPhase, interventionModel, blindingSchema, every arm, every epoch, every objective, every endpoint, and every eligibility criterion. It is optional elsewhere.

# 5. Reviewer summary

Write `usdm-summary.md` — what a reviewer reads to decide approve vs revise. Include: the study title and phase; a table of arms; the epoch chain; a table of objectives with their endpoints; inclusion/exclusion criteria counts with the first few of each; what you could NOT resolve and why; and your confidence with its rationale. Keep it skimmable — this is a review aid, not a reproduction of usdm.json.

# 6. Revise re-entry

If `steps['review-usdm']` is present in your Input Data, this is a revision. Read `steps['review-usdm'].comment` (and `reviewerCallToAction` if present) — that comment is the source of truth for this iteration. Correct ONLY the items the reviewer flagged, keep everything else stable, and add a `revisionLog` array to result.json recording `{ "comment": "...", "changed": ["<path>", ...] }`. Do not return the prior iteration unchanged.

# OUTPUT CONTRACT (MANDATORY)

Write all three deliverables to BOTH locations — `/workspace/usdm/` is committed to the run branch, `/output/` is what surfaces as this step's Output Files in the run UI:

```
mkdir -p /workspace/usdm
# write usdm.json, usdm-provenance.json, usdm-summary.md into /workspace/usdm/
cp /workspace/usdm/usdm.json /workspace/usdm/usdm-provenance.json /workspace/usdm/usdm-summary.md /output/
```

Then write `/output/result.json` — this is the step's output value, so keep it small (no USDM payload inside it):

```json
{
  "nctId": "NCT...",
  "usdmVersion": "3.0.0",
  "studyTitle": "<official title>",
  "studyPhase": "<decode, e.g. Phase III Trial>",
  "sourceDocuments": [ { "filename": "...", "typeAbbrev": "Prot", "pages": 214, "usedAs": "primary" } ],
  "counts": { "titles": 0, "studyIdentifiers": 0, "arms": 0, "epochs": 0, "elements": 0, "studyCells": 0, "objectives": 0, "endpoints": 0, "inclusionCriteria": 0, "exclusionCriteria": 0, "studyInterventions": 0, "activities": 0 },
  "integrityCheck": { "passed": true, "danglingReferences": [] },
  "unresolved": [ { "path": "study.versions[0].studyDesigns[0].activities", "reason": "SoA table did not extract legibly from the scanned appendix" } ],
  "outputFiles": ["usdm.json", "usdm-provenance.json", "usdm-summary.md"],
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "confidence_rationale": "...",
  "summary": "<one line>"
}
```

Your FINAL message must be ONLY this, with no other text:
`{"output_file": "/output/result.json", "summary": "<one line>"}`

steps.name: Review USDM Metadata
steps.description: Review the extracted USDM metadata. Read usdm-summary.md first, then spot-check usdm.json against usdm-provenance.json — every title, phase, arm, epoch, objective, endpoint and eligibility criterion carries a source file and page number. Check the `unresolved` list in the step output for what the agent could not find. Approve to finish, or request changes to send the run back to Generate USDM Metadata with your comment.

params.name: comment
params.description: What to fix in the USDM metadata (required when requesting changes). Be specific about paths, e.g. "arms are wrong — the protocol has 3 arms, see page 24".
